theorems.name: Cantor
theorems.title: Cantor's diagonal argument
theorems.blurb: No function `f` from `α` onto the predicates on `α` (its subsets): some set is always missed. Suppose `f` were onto and build the diagonal set — the points `x` with `¬ f x x`, not in their own image. Some `d` reaches it, and asking whether `f d d` holds contradicts itself either way.

theorems.name: ZeroAdd
theorems.title: Zero plus n
theorems.blurb: On `Nat`, addition recurses on its second argument, so `n + 0 = n` holds by definition but `0 + n = n` does not: it needs induction. `omega` and `simp` know it already; `induction n` shows why it is true.

theorems.name: Double
theorems.title: Doubling, by induction
theorems.blurb: A function defined by recursion, and a fact about it that no automation knows yet: `double n = 2 * n`. Induct on `n`, unfold one step of `double`, and let `omega` finish with the induction hypothesis.

theorems.name: AndSwap
theorems.title: And is symmetric
theorems.blurb: From `p ∧ q`, prove `q ∧ p`: take the hypothesis apart, then build the conjunction one side at a time.
theorems.statement: ∀ (p q : Prop), p ∧ q → q ∧ p

theorems.name: OrSwap
theorems.title: Or is symmetric
theorems.blurb: From `p ∨ q`, prove `q ∨ p`: there are two ways the hypothesis could hold, so there are two cases, and each picks a side of the goal.
theorems.statement: ∀ (p q : Prop), p ∨ q → q ∨ p

theorems.name: ZeroOrPos
theorems.title: Zero or positive
theorems.blurb: Every natural number is `0` or a successor. `cases n` splits the goal in two, one per constructor; each side then picks its half of the `∨`.

theorems.name: SquareParity
theorems.title: A square has its root's parity
theorems.blurb: `n * n` and `n` leave the same remainder mod 2. `omega` cannot see it — it does linear arithmetic, and `n * n` is not linear — so split on the remainder of `n` and compute.

theorems.name: AppendLength
theorems.title: The length of an append
theorems.blurb: Induction on a list: one case for the empty list, one for `x :: xs`, with the hypothesis about `xs` in hand. `simp` knows the whole fact already.
theorems.statement: ∀ (xs ys : List Nat), (xs ++ ys).length = xs.length + ys.length

theorems.name: SevenSquared
theorems.title: A witness
theorems.blurb: To prove `∃ n, n * n = 49`, name the `n`: `refine ⟨7, ?_⟩` leaves the check `7 * 7 = 49`, which is a computation. Guess wrong and Lean says so.

theorems.name: NoLargest
theorems.title: No largest number
theorems.blurb: For every `n` there is a bigger `m`. The witness may depend on `n`: take `n + 1`, and the rest is arithmetic.

theorems.name: RewriteChain
theorems.title: A chain of rewrites
theorems.blurb: Two equations and a `+ 0`: rewrite the goal one step at a time — drop the `+ 0`, replace `a` by `b`, then `b` by `c` — until both sides agree.
theorems.statement: ∀ (a b c : Nat), a = b → b = c → a + 0 = c

theorems.name: Absurd
theorems.title: From a false hypothesis
theorems.blurb: `n + 1 = 0` never holds, so from it anything follows — even `2 + 2 = 5`. The work is in the hypothesis, not the goal.

theorems.name: NoSqrtTwo
theorems.title: No square root of 2 mod 5
theorems.blurb: `x * x ≠ 2` for every `x` in `Fin 5`: there are five cases, so `decide` checks them all. Introduce `x` first and `decide` has a variable it cannot evaluate.
